A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same visual-alignment study and ShareLock method. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison despite substantial reformatting and some internal reporting inconsistencies.

before.justification: V2 reports original visual-generalization experiments, ShareLock benchmark evaluations, component ablations, and qualitative retrieval results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds controlled encoder-decoder comparisons, projection experiments, and a batch-capacity comparison.

M1.justification: ShareLock retains frozen vision and language backbones, contrastive text-to-vision alignment, a linear projection for probing, and a four-layer, 4096-dimensional MLP for general-purpose VLM training. The additional projection directions, depths, and pooling choices are comparative experiments rather than changes to the proposed default method.

E1.justification: The four visual-generalization datasets, COCO/CC3M/CC12M training coverage, classification benchmarks, multilingual evaluation, Winoground, and retrieval tasks remain. The added experiments vary models and controls within retained coverage. Aircraft and ESAT remain evaluated elsewhere despite omitted columns in the consolidated backbone table.

E2.justification: Section 4 adds a one-hot class-representation baseline and comparisons using paired Ettin encoders and decoders. The conventional VLM comparator sets remain unchanged. Table 1 relabels T5-XL as SentenceT5-XL, but Table 11 identifies T5-3b; this inconsistency does not reliably establish an additional comparator replacement.

E3.justification: V3 introduces controlled encoder-decoder comparisons matching pretraining data and parameter counts across six sizes, with additional pooling comparisons. It also adds an 80GB memory-budget comparison and systematic projection-direction/depth configurations. These substantially extend the evaluation design, while the retained benchmark splits, accuracy metrics, and 3.5k/5k-step training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses test whether semantic class information is necessary, whether decoder advantages survive matched data and model sizes, how pooling affects that comparison, and how projection direction and depth affect generalization. Table 5 additionally examines memory capacity. Existing vision-backbone analyses are consolidated into Section 5.4 rather than newly introduced; the earlier fine-tuning, transformer-projection, and loss comparisons remain.

E5.justification: Tables 11 and 12 add ± values to dataset-level means previously reported without uncertainty. Both versions already specify five initialization seeds and averaging across those seeds, so additional runs are not established. V3 does not define whether the ± quantities represent standard deviations, standard errors, or another measure.

E6.justification: V3 adds the one-hot baseline's 4.5% score, the Ettin decoder advantage averaging 2.7 percentage points, and the memory-capacity and projection results in Tables 5 and 7. Table 11 changes Wikipedia-based ImageNet+ scores for ModernBERT from 24.8 to 18.3 and all-roberta-v1 from 41.7 to 31.8, with corresponding averages revised to 23.2 and 39.23. Consolidation removes some backbone-specific Aircraft/ESAT entries and changes the reported scaling summaries. Main benchmark Tables 2–4 retain their scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation remains equivalent. Renaming seen/unseen classes as aligned/unaligned classes and expressing Equation 2 through explicit cosine similarity clarify existing definitions and normalization. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction newly claim that decoder advantages persist when controlling for pretraining data and model size. The abstract drops the earlier 'first direct analysis' priority claim and highlights existing efficiency results. The principal visual-alignment, language-performance correlation, and ShareLock contributions remain.

C2.justification: Section 4 moves beyond v2's explanation based mainly on model and dataset scale to suggest an advantage from autoregressive pretraining under controlled comparisons. Section 5.4 adds explanations involving greater semantic coherence of vision embeddings, visually irrelevant linguistic information, and overfitting when both modalities are projected. The earlier compositionality, Phi-3, and principal limitations discussions are largely retained.

D1.justification: V3 explicitly identifies the default Llama-3 8B/DINOv2-L backbones, specifies BERT-Base for LiT, and adds model parameter counts. It also documents cached-label inference and an approximately 160-GFLOP estimate for ViT-L/14 at 224×224. These are documentation additions; the existing feature-precomputation costs, training details, and project-page target remain.

R1.justification: V3 adds Weller et al. (2025), the Ettin paired-model work, and removes the Raffel et al. T5 reference accompanying the changed Table 1 attribution. It also softens the abstract's explicit priority claim. The related-work section and broader positioning against prior visual-understanding and alignment research remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract and selected introductory and methodological passages are rewritten, and seen/unseen terminology becomes aligned/unaligned. Section 5.4 expands into Component Analysis, incorporating the earlier appendix vision-backbone discussion. Limitations move from Section 7 to Appendix B. The main narrative and most existing prose remain recognizable.

P2.justification: V3 changes the document from two-column to single-column TMLR layout, adds the training-protocol diagram and Ettin plot, and redraws the method-comparison diagram. New memory, projection, and Ettin tables accompany consolidation of earlier backbone tables into Table 6. Legends, captions, table headers, and placements change extensively. Existing qualitative retrieval images and scores are retained.

improvement.justification: The matched Ettin comparisons, semantic baseline, and projection ablations strengthen support for the architectural interpretations and design choices, while added uncertainty values improve transparency. These gains are tempered by undefined ± notation and new inconsistencies between Table 1 and Table 11: the latter revises Wikipedia averages to 23.2 and 39.23 while the former retains 24.8 and 41.7. Overall, v3 provides better evidence but only a qualified improvement in reporting quality.
